patients.label: Preterm male infant with congenital tuberculous lymphadenitis born to a mother with pulmonary TB

identity_evidence.quote: a preterm male infant (30 weeks’ gestation)

attribution_limitations: Respiratory distress is placed at presentation at 3 weeks in the abstract but described as developing at 9 weeks of age in the case narrative.

One sentence gives initiation doses (isoniazid 10 mg/kg/day, pyrazinamide 30 mg/kg/day) and then, as adjusted for prematurity, isoniazid 8.3 mg/kg and pyrazinamide 25 mg/kg; rifampicin is 10 mg/kg in both. It is unclear whether the adjusted doses replaced the first ones at initiation or were given later.
The text states dosing used the WHO weight band for 3 to < 4 kg while giving the weight at ATT start as 1.7 kg.
The microbiology timing sentence in the key-clues list refers to positive TB-PCR (Xpert MTB) or culture from lymph node aspirate, while lymph node culture was not performed.

Ages for the antibiotic course (5 weeks of age), ICU admission (12 weeks of age) and result timing are printed in parentheses and are not fully consistent with the stated durations; relations between the respiratory episode and the ENT referral are not stated.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Submandibular lymphadenopathy.

limitations: Ultrasound and histopathology images are not included in the article; only Figure 1 (clinical photograph) is available.
The case narrative states that ultrasound measures, abdominal imaging, laboratory ranges, oxygen saturations and heart rate at key points were not available.

Mother is not a separate roster patient; her history is recorded with subject mother. The source says her own records were not accessed and her history came from a referral note after interviewing the caregiver.

Respiratory distress onset (3 weeks in the abstract versus 9 weeks of age in the narrative) is a source conflict kept review-only; initial versus prematurity-adjusted ATT doses are ambiguous (which was given) and kept review-only.
Parenthetical ages for the antibiotic course, ICU admission and Xpert result are kept literal; the source does not say whether they mark the start or the end of each interval.
Caregiver comments, Cantwell criteria text, WHO guideline statements and the discussion are background and not recorded as patient facts.
